Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Maternal dTpa during each pregnancy and adolescent dTpa at 12–13 years are in the national programme.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: The 60% and 75% inputs are projections. AIR coverage by ages 13 or 15 measures cumulative receipt, including later catch-up; the model schedules its event at age 12.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Maternal Tdap is recommended from 16 weeks; the routine teenage Td/IPV programme has no pertussis component.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: The 73% maternal anchor matches the 2025–2026 financial-year estimate. Proposed adolescent pertussis vaccination adds a programme.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Maternal vaccination is recommended from 16 weeks; the adolescent booster is offered in school grades 8–9.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: Main inputs of 50% and 90% are projections. The 2025 pregnancy register records 68% vaccinated, including unknown status in the denominator. Fifth-dose completion at age 16 was 93%, a different measure from the model's age-15 event.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Routine vaccination at 11–12 years uses DT; optional DPT vaccination is documented.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: Zero denotes the national routine-programme baseline; optional private doses are a separate source of uptake. A JIHS report describing November 2025 stated that Tdap was unapproved domestically. Modelled introductions therefore require explicit future product assumptions.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Tdap is offered in each pregnancy and at age 11.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: Main inputs are 75% and 80%. The official 2025 maternal annual figure of 64.1% supplied a separate future anchor. The age-11 input specifies prospective model coverage.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: The childhood DTaP schedule from 2025 includes doses at 2, 4, 6 and 18 months and 6 years.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: Maternal and adolescent introductions are hypothetical additions to this schedule. Adult and pregnancy product indications form separate programme decisions.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: Maternal dTpa is offered from 20 weeks; the routine adolescent/adult schedule uses dT without pertussis.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: The 75% maternal input is a projection. The administrative coverage definition uses dTpa doses in women aged 15–45 divided by live births, which differs from linked vaccination during pregnancy.

Programme evidence relevant to the compa: The maternal programme offers monovalent aP, with combined-vaccine substitutions specified in guidance. Grade-6 vaccination remained dT in the 2026 schedule.
Interpretation of baseline coverage: The 50% maternal anchor is assumed. Published regional delivery-cohort coverage was retained as regional evidence. The common maternal protection mechanism across products is a modelling assumption.
